slot.brief: Solve a first-order linear ODE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) with an integrating factor; identify P, multiply, integrate.

stem: The general solution of the differential equation dy/dx + y tan x = sin 2x is:
options: y = C cos x + 2 sin^2 x
y = C cos x - 2 cos^2 x
y = C sec x - 2 cos x
y = C sin x - 2 sin^2 x

verdicts.working: The integrating factor is sec x. Thus (y sec x)' = sec x sin 2x = 2 sin x, so y sec x = -2 cos x + C, giving y = C cos x - 2 cos² x.

working:
Here P(x) = tan x, so the integrating factor is exp(integral of tan x dx) = sec x. Multiplying gives (d/dx)(y sec x) = sin(2x) sec x = 2 sin x. Integrating, y sec x = -2 cos x + C. Hence y = C cos x - 2 cos^2 x.

Independent check: The integrating factor is sec x. Thus (y sec x)' = sec x sin 2x = 2 sin x, so y sec x = -2 cos x + C, giving y = C cos x - 2 cos² x.
solution:
The integrating factor is $e^{\int \tan x\,dx}=\sec x$. Hence
$$\frac{d}{dx}(y\sec x)=\sec x\sin 2x=2\sin x.$$
Integrating gives $y\sec x=-2\cos x+C$, so $\boxed{y=C\cos x-2\cos^2 x}$. (B)
